# StoreUpdateRowsNL's animation-mark check fails in CI while the batched values repaint

## Context

Today `test/playwright/e2e/grid/StoreUpdateRowsNL.spec.mjs` (#20975, for #20968) failed four times in CI on its animation-mark check, and on nothing else:
- the dev push of `a29510a067`: run 43872820052, e2e-engine shard 12/14. Dev was green at `2404340dfa` (run 43835747256), and the three commits between them touch no grid code.
- neo #21087 at `37553c911b`, also shard 12/14, and neo #21044. Neither PR touches the grid.
- the first run of neo #21118, whose body records it.

```
Error: each changed counter cell was marked
- Expected  - 5
+ Received  + 1        (received: [])
```

## The Problem

The spec writes three visible rows and two off-screen rows in one `updateRows` batch. In every failing run the values arrive: the `readRow` poll before the mark check passes. But the MutationObserver that records each `.neo-animated` counter cell sees none of the three.

Either the engine drops the mark (a changed cell does not flash), or the spec observes too early. Which one is not known.

## The Architectural Reality

- `Neo.grid.column.AnimatedChange#onRecordChange` (`src/grid/column/AnimatedChange.mjs:77`) follows `recordChange`. It waits 20 ms, resolves the row with `body.getRow(record)`, adds `neo-animated` to the cell's vdom and calls `row.update()`.
- `Neo.grid.Body#onStoreRowsChange` rebuilds each changed mounted row's vdom at once and sends one `body.update()` with `updateDepth = -1`.
- `Neo.grid.Body#getRow(record)` maps `store.indexOf(record)` to a pool row as `rowIndex % items.length`, inside `mountedRows`. `AnimatedChange` then finds the cell by `body.getCellId(row.rowIndex, dataField)`. A pool row whose `rowIndex` differs from the record's index yields no cell, and so no mark.
- A `row.update()` that collides with an in-flight ancestor update is queued as a post-update (`Neo.mixin.VdomLifecycle#isParentUpdating` → `Neo.manager.VDomUpdate#registerPostUpdate`), not dropped.
- Locally, with the CPU throttled 6× (CDP `Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate`, which slows the main thread and not the workers), 3 of 3 runs marked all three rows, and the rows were in the DOM before the batch. The failure did not reproduce.
- A deterministic control by @neo-gpt-emmy, at `a29510a067`: holding the batch repaint's vdom flight for 120 ms while a concurrent `body.createViewData(false, true)` runs misses all three marks, 3 of 3. A candidate that drops the 20 ms timer and awaits `row.promiseUpdate()` before marking, re-validating the row, its record and the store, marks all three, 3 of 3. The mark is lost when a re-render of the row overlaps the timer.

## The Fix

The cause is in the engine: the mark lives only in a patched row vdom, so a rebuild before the patch is sent drops it (the deterministic control above). Make the mark render state:
1. `Neo.grid.Row#applyRendererOutput` asks a column for its cells' state classes through an optional `getCellStateCls(rendererConfig)` hook, after the `cellCls` config. `Column.Base` stays as it is, so duck-typed columns keep working.
2. `Neo.grid.column.AnimatedChange` keeps the records it marked, by store key, for `markDuration` ms. Its `getCellStateCls()` returns their classes, so every render inside the window carries the mark.
   - A repeat change inside the window toggles `neo-animated-alt`, which switches the keyframes and restarts the animation.
   - A batch record needs no patch, because the batch's repaint renders the mark.
   - A single edit patches the rendered cell as before, without the 20 ms timer.
3. `AnimatedChange.scss` and `AnimatedCurrency.scss` declare the `-alt` keyframes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The cause is named with evidence from a failing run or a deterministic reproduction, not inferred.
- [ ] A changed cell keeps its mark through a re-render inside the window. An e2e arm runs the forced `createViewData` during the batch repaint and is red on `dev` before the fix.
- [ ] A repeat change inside the window restarts the animation, and AnimatedCurrency keeps its negative and positive marks (unit).
- [ ] A batch marks its rows through its own repaint, with no extra row update per marked cell (unit).
- [ ] `StoreUpdateRowsNL.spec`'s mark check is unchanged and passes.

## Out of Scope

The batch semantics of `Store#updateRows` (#20968), and `AnimatedChange`'s visual design.

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-11-16T13:48:48Z

A design note before implementing. Awaiting `row.promiseUpdate()` per marked cell (the control's candidate) has a cost: `Neo.mixin.VdomLifecycle#promiseUpdate` always renders. Its JSDoc says a change made after a flight collected its payload "belongs to the next one". So each animated change gains one row render on top of its mark render. For a batch of n changed rows, that is about n extra row renders, in the live-data grids' hot path.

Two shapes to measure against the control before choosing:
1. **Wait only for a pending repaint.** After a microtask, so a repaint of the same tick has run, await the row's flight only while one is pending (`isVdomUpdating`, `needsVdomUpdate`). An idle row then costs nothing extra.
2. **Make the mark render state.** The column keeps the records it marked until the animation ends, and its cell renderer adds the class. Any re-render inside that window, a scroll pass included, then keeps the mark, which removes the race for every repaint.

Either one also needs a `catch`, because destroying a row rejects its parked `promiseUpdate()`. Shape 1 is the smaller change; shape 2 closes the race for every source of repaint. I'll measure both with the control's delay injection, and the render counts, before picking one.
